macro.regime: Iran pause (3rd night) sinks oil -9%; silver rebounds; hawkish-hold Fed decides 29 Jul
macro.narrative: Re-verified Tue 28 Jul 07:00 SGT (pre-Asia-open) against the Mon 27 Jul US close. The weekend de-escalation held and extended: the US and Iran paused strikes for a THIRD straight night, with Washington giving diplomacy 'space' after ~13 nights of strikes — and the oil premium collapsed. Brent fell -8.7% to ~$88.36 and WTI -7.5% to ~$82.61 on Monday (a sharp reversal from last week's >9% gain that had taken Brent to ~$102), which unwound the inflation impulse that had driven the rate-hike fear. That relieved the rate-sensitive book squarely: silver rebounded ~+2.3% to ~$59.4 (Sep futures ~$59.81) and rose on the day/week/month/year for the first time since May; gold firmed ~+0.7% to ~$4,098. US equities were mixed at record-ish levels — S&P 500 +0.02% to a record 7,413, Dow +0.51% to 52,210 on the oil retreat, but Nasdaq -0.18% (24,932) as NVDA fell ~5% and SanDisk -11% on memory weakness kept the AI-capex/semis unwind alive. Crypto caught the risk-relief bid (BTC ~$64.8-65.3k, ETH ~+4.4% to ~$1,950). Rate-hike odds cooled with oil: CME now prices ~1-in-3 (~33%) for a hike at the 28-29 Jul FOMC (down from a ~38-40% peak last Thursday), with September hike odds still ~80%; Chair Warsh runs a hawkish, no-guidance regime and the decision lands Wed 29 Jul 2pm ET (no SEP). Credit stays calm (HY OAS ~269bp), longer-term breadth healthy (~69% >200-DMA) but no longer broadening; positioning stretched-bullish (BofA July FMS cash 3.6% = contrarian Cash-Rule sell). China's 24 Jul Politburo stimulus signal remains a live positive for the HK-tech sleeve. The single biggest cross-book swing is now whether the Iran pause holds (keeps oil down, unwinds rate-hike fear — tailwind for levered silver, S-REITs, HK tech, crypto) or breaks down (re-spikes oil/gold and hardens the Fed's hawkish tilt). Watch: the 29 Jul FOMC decision, Q2 US GDP/PCE this week, the AI-capex/semis unwind (NVDA -5%), the end-July MAS S-REIT review, and the Iran diplomatic thread.

drivers.factor: US-Iran war: THIRD-night strike pause; oil premium collapses -9%
drivers.read: The pause held for a THIRD straight night with Washington giving diplomacy 'space' — and the oil premium collapsed: Brent -8.7% to ~$88.36, WTI -7.5% to ~$82.61 Monday, a sharp reversal of last week's spike to ~$102. That unwinds the inflation/rate-hike fear that pressured the rate-sensitive book — a net tailwind for levered silver (which rebounded ~+2.3%), S-REITs, HK tech and crypto, at the cost of the small energy long. The tail risk is the pause breaking down and re-spiking oil/gold; a Strait-of-Hormuz closure is the extreme case. Iran denied a reported 10-day ceasefire, so the truce is fragile.

As oil collapsed on the Iran pause, CME hike odds for the 29 Jul FOMC cooled to ~1-in-3 (~33%, from a ~38-40% peak last Thursday), with September hike odds still ~80%. That relief let silver rebound ~+2.3% to ~$59.4 (up on the day/week/month/year for the first time since May) and gold firm ~+0.7% to ~$4,098. This real-yield/dollar channel remains the book's swing factor into the Fed; silver's 2-3x beta to hike expectations cuts both ways around the 29 Jul print (no SEP, Warsh hawkish/no-guidance).

Benchmark-weight with a quality/large-cap tilt; keep dry powder for a post-FOMC shakeout.

Still the clearest OW, and the internal split resolved toward metals: the Iran pause sank oil (Brent -8.7% to ~$88, WTI -7.5% to ~$82.6 Mon), gutting the war premium that had led energy — but the same de-escalation is exactly what relieves the metals. Silver rebounded ~+2.3% to ~$59.4 (first up day/week/month/year since May) and gold firmed to ~$4,098. Metals now have the rate/dollar impulse fading in their favor; energy is the near-term loser of the pause.

Trading purely off the macro rate/yield channel — and the Iran-pause risk relief lifted it: BTC held ~$64.8-65.3k and ETH jumped ~+4.4% to ~$1,950 Monday as the oil/rate fear eased. Moves in lockstep with the silver/REIT rate-sensitivity trade. The EU's 21st Russia-sanctions package tightening offshore crypto rails is a lingering overhang. Keep sizing small, favor BTC over alts; convexity improves further on a Fed pivot.

10Y at a year-high ~4.71% offers real carry, but the oil-driven headline-inflation risk and a hike-biased Fed cap duration upside near-term. HY OAS ~268bp is tight — a thin cushion. Favor the belly/quality IG (which drew +$17.2bn the week to 1 Jul) for carry over the long end and low-quality HY; a growth scare or Iran de-escalation would reward duration.

DXY firmed ~101.5 on the war/rate-hike bid, and cash yields ~3.5-3.75% at the fed-funds floor give positive carry and optionality — the big cash pile is productive dry powder for a post-FOMC metals/rare-earth shakeout, an asset in this regime. Neutral on two-way USD direction into the Fed.
